def: A precise statement of what is predicted, for which unit, at what time, from which features, and for which decision.
A measurable stand-in used as the target when the quantity you care about cannot be observed, which carries its own flaws into the model.
A table counting predictions by predicted class and true class, giving true and false positives and negatives.
Of the cases the model flagged as positive, the fraction that really are positive.
Of the cases that really are positive, the fraction the model flagged; also called sensitivity or true positive rate.
The harmonic mean of precision and recall, which is low whenever either is low.
The score above which a case is flagged as positive; a separate choice from the model that produces the score.
The probability that a random positive case scores higher than a random negative case, summarising ranking quality across all thresholds.
The mean of the precision values at each rank where a true positive appears, approximating the area under the precision-recall curve.
The fraction of positives among the k highest-scored cases, matching decisions limited by review capacity.
The rule to flag a case when its probability exceeds the false-alarm cost divided by the sum of the false-alarm and miss costs.
Root mean squared error, a regression metric in the units of the target whose best constant prediction is the mean.
Mean absolute error, a regression metric whose best constant prediction is the median.
An asymmetric absolute-error loss whose minimiser is a chosen quantile of the outcome distribution.
The tendency of a measure to stop reflecting its purpose once it is used as a target to optimise.
